clue.text: Such a baby is naturally inconceivable

definitions.text: Such a baby is naturally inconceivable

parts.words: Such a baby is naturally inconceivable
parts.note: a baby conceived in a laboratory dish could not have been conceived the natural way, so it is 'naturally inconceivable'

explanation.surface: A remark that some baby could never happen by nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inconceivable' looks like it means unthinkable, but here it means literally not conceived naturally: the IVF baby of the 1970s headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: IVF children were popularly called by this name because fertilisation happened in laboratory glassware.

clue.text: Spaniel taking tail off amphibian

indicators.note: taking tail off means the synonym loses its last letter

parts.note: a spaniel figuratively is a fawning, servile follower, a toady

explanation.surface: A dog losing its tail is likened to a frog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spaniel' looks like the dog but is its figurative sense, a cringing flatterer.
explanation.definitionFit: A warty land-dwelling creature related to frogs belongs to the amphibians.

clue.text: Cakes in batches

definitions.meaning: a verb: cakes harden or set solid, as mud does

explanation.surface: Cakes being baked in batches.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly or cement firms up, as mud cakes; a set is a group or collection.

clue.text: Person who scares easily, if trapped by dog

indicators.note: trapped by means the little word is held inside the dog's name

parts.note: a terrier is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A timid person whose nerve is caught by a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'easily' joins the pieces and only colours the surface, suggesting a timid person; 'trapped by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: One who frightens others, someone causing terror.

clue.text: Family shoots extortioners

parts.note: blood means family or kin, as in 'blood is thicker than water'
suckers are shoots springing from a plant's root or stem

explanation.surface: Relatives fire a gun at blackmailers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoots' looks like a verb but is the noun, plant growths.
explanation.definitionFit: People who drain others of money, like leeches, are called this figuratively.

clue.text: Briefly debate athletic event

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to debate a matter is to discuss it

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a quick argument about a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' removes the last S of DISCUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrown-plate contest is one of the field events in athletics.

clue.text: Lazy person taking the wheel

definitions.meaning: an idle wheel transmits motion between two gears without driving

explanation.surface: A layabout takes the driving seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking the' just joins the definitions; in machinery an idle pulley or gear between two others has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer; also the engineering term for an intermediate pulley or gearwheel.

clue.text: Fish arrives — and chips

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to enter is to come in, to arrive

explanation.surface: A fish turns up, and so do the chips, in a fish-and-chip supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chips' is not fried potato but British slang for woodworkers: 'Chips' is a nickname for a ship's carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips is old naval and British slang for a woodworker, from the wood chips they make.

clue.text: Seat that a woman may be forced by habit to take

definitions.text: Seat that a woman may be forced by habit to take

parts.words: Seat that a woman may be forced by habit to take
parts.note: a habit is a riding outfit, whose long skirt forced women riders to sit with both legs on one side of the horse

explanation.surface: A woman stuck by custom in one particular chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' looks like custom, but it is a riding habit, the long-skirted outfit women once rode in.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding position with both legs on one side of the horse, once required of women.

clue.text: After an advance, fell back to waiting area

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the advance in the answer

parts.note: an ante is a stake paid in advance in poker

indicators.note: back means the synonym for fell is read in reverse

parts.note: a fell is a stretch of upland moor in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone retreats to a waiting room after making a move forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb (fell back = retreated), but it is the noun, a moor; 'back' turns MOOR into ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room leading to a main one, where visitors wait to be received.

clue.text: Disposed of by burning, as bags may be

definitions.meaning: surplus gas at a refinery is burnt off in a flame, which is called this
Oxford bags are wide trousers, and such trousers widen out towards the hem

explanation.surface: Waste gets burnt off, and trousers may have wide legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' are not sacks but baggy trousers, Oxford bags, a British style with very wide legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste gas is flamed off at oil rigs; bell-bottom trousers widen towards the ankle.

clue.text: Asleep before undressing? That's being ahead!

indicators.note: before places the first piece above the second in this down answer

parts.note: out means unconscious or asleep, as in out like a light
stripping is taking off clothes

explanation.surface: Someone nods off before getting undressed, and claims to be winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtaking or surpassing others means moving in front of them.

clue.text: Farm worker given accommodation in the rear

parts.note: hind is an old Scottish and northern word for a skilled farm labourer
quarters are lodgings or living accommodation

explanation.surface: A farm hand is housed at the back of the property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the rear' looks like part of the farm scene, but it is the definition: an animal's back end.
explanation.definitionFit: The back legs and rump of a four-legged animal, hence the backside generally.

clue.text: Wine put in container at bottom of cave

indicators.note: in a down answer, at bottom of puts the container beneath the word for cave

parts.note: a chamber is a cavity, a natural cave or hollow underground
a tin is a metal container

explanation.surface: Wine is stored in a vessel at the base of a cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' is a link: put TIN at the bottom of CHAMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated red Burgundy from the Côte de Nuits, a grand cru vineyard.

clue.text: Ruined state of Evelyn, lacking capital and coins?

definitions.text: Ruined state of Evelyn, lacking capital and coins?

indicators.note: ruined means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order
lacking capital means the name loses its capital letter, the opening E

explanation.surface: Evelyn is broke, without money or coins.
explanation.walkthrough: VELYN plus COINS is anagrammed; the whole clue also describes being bankrupt, lacking capital and cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Bankruptcy, the condition of being unable to pay debts.

clue.text: Greeting a small number inside Asian capital

indicators.note: inside means the article and the abbreviation are placed within the greeting word

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
No. is the short form of number

explanation.surface: Someone says hello to a handful of people in an Asian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Morally pure, unlike Dick?

definitions.meaning: without a stain on one's character
spotted dick is a British steamed suet pudding studded with currants, so something not like it has no spots

explanation.surface: A virtuous person is contrasted with a man called Dick.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted dick is a traditional British suet pudding dotted with dried fruit; 'Dick' looks like a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A stainless reputation is one without blemish; a pudding without currants would lack spots.

clue.text: Boy's ashore, initially, when things are quiet

indicators.note: initially says the word for ashore comes first in the answer, ahead of the boy

parts.note: on land is off the sea
a son is a boy; the possessive gives no letter

explanation.surface: A boy comes ashore first, during a quiet spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letters signal but just puts OFF SEA before SON.
explanation.definitionFit: The slack time of year for a holiday trade, when few visitors come.

clue.text: In berth, fix new angle for mast or sail

indicators.note: in means the new angle is placed within the word for berth

parts.note: to moor a boat is to berth it
the rake of a mast is its angle of slope from the vertical

explanation.surface: A sailor at berth adjusts the tilt of a mast or sail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fix' and 'or' are link words; 'In' is the container signal. The definition is just 'sail', not 'mast or sail'.
explanation.definitionFit: A light square topsail set above the skysail on old sailing ships.

clue.text: Wild rose's first in leaf, unusually

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters are arranged in an unusual order
first picks the opening letter of the word rose

explanation.surface: A wild rose's first bloom appears in an odd leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: R joins LEAF and the five letters are anagrammed by 'unusually'.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal gone back to living untamed in nature, after domestication, is described this way.

clue.text: The one who left the First Lady to catch a snooper

indicators.note: to catch means the word for the First Lady holds the article inside it

parts.note: Eve, the first woman in Genesis, with the possessive giving EVES
someone who drops another, leaving them, can be called a dropper

explanation.surface: A man abandons the President's wife in order to catch a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' looks like a president's wife but is Eve, the first woman; read as 'Eve's dropper', the one who dropped Eve, it captures A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who secretly listens in on others' private conversations is a snoop.

clue.text: In which, primarily, Scandinavian adults undergo naked ablutions?

definitions.text: In which, primarily, Scandinavian adults undergo naked ablutions?

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A question about where Nordic grown-ups bathe nude.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of the last five words spell the answer, and the clue as a whole describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finnish steam bath where people traditionally bathe unclothed.

clue.text: Maiden is, before acquiring first of spouses

definitions.text: Maiden is, before acquiring first of spouses

parts.note: M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word spouses

explanation.surface: A girl remains single until she gains a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' and 'acquiring' just place the pieces; the whole clue also describes an unmarried young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of an unmarried woman, a young lady not yet wed.

clue.text: Slipped disk resulting from slide? Just the opposite

indicators.note: slipped means the letters have slipped out of place

explanation.surface: A slipped disc caused by sliding, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' says the slide results from the slipped letters of DISK, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle sliding out of control on a slippery road.

clue.text: Language used in Oxford

definitions.meaning: a language or form of speech
an Oxford is a lace-up shoe, and the flap under its laces is part of it

explanation.surface: A language spoken at the University of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is not the city or university but an oxford shoe, which has a flap under the laces.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech of a people is a language; the shoe flap under laces bears the same name.

clue.text: Fool employed to check depth

definitions.meaning: slang for a stupid person, an idiot
a graduated rod dipped into a tank or engine to measure the level of liquid

explanation.surface: An idiot is put to work checking how deep something is.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an idiot; also the measuring rod used to check engine oil level.

clue.text: How Americans deny any wrong, for example

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of the little word are put the wrong way round

parts.note: say introduces an example, as in 'a city, say, Paris'

explanation.surface: A note on the way Americans dismiss any error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns ANY into NAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainly American usage for refusing or opposing; to vote no or to reject.

clue.text: Tormented, as Iago's end turned out

indicators.note: turned out signals that the letters get turned around into a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive S counts here as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A remark on how badly Iago fared at the close of Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link; the eight letters of IAGOS and END are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffering great anguish or torture, physical or mental.
